findings.issue: を is the object marker here, but the literal renders クッキーを with the topic device 'As for...', misteaching を as if it were は. The expl and tokens correctly call クッキー the object; the literal contradicts them.
findings.current: As for the cookie, (take) one, please.

findings.issue: 'Quanto a...' is the corpus device for the topic particle は, but the particle here is object を; the literal misrepresents the structure (expl/tokens correctly treat クッキー as objeto marcado por を).
findings.current: Quanto ao biscoito, (pegue) um, por favor.

findings.issue: Particle を left as を; the corpus phonetic convention writes particles as pronounced (を→お), as applied to は→わ elsewhere in this batch. Inconsistent with the convention.
findings.current: くっきーをおひとつどうぞ。
findings.suggested: くっきーおおひとつどうぞ。

findings.issue: tokens[0]-[1] are orphaned all-null fragments of 申し上げる placed BEFORE 私, out of sentence position and duplicating the real token 申し上げる (index 6). Concatenating token surfaces no longer reconstructs the sentence.
findings.current: tokens begin: 申し (all null), 上げる (all null), then 私, から…
findings.suggested: Delete stray fragment tokens 0-1 (申し, 上げる); the dissection should start at 私.

findings.issue: tokens[0]-[1] (ユーザー, 名) are all-null fragments duplicating the following merged token ユーザー名; concatenating token surfaces yields ユーザー名 twice, corrupting the dissection. Same artifact as in sent:tatoeba-3501339.
findings.current: tokens begin: ユーザー (all null), 名 (all null), then ユーザー名 (glossed)
findings.suggested: Delete duplicate fragment tokens 0-1 (ユーザー, 名); keep the merged ユーザー名 token.

findings.issue: Agreement error: predicate 'está incorreto' (masc. sing.) clashes with the nearest subject 'a senha' (fem.). Standard pt-BR software wording uses plural agreement with 'ou' (or nearest-agreement 'está incorreta').
findings.current: O nome de usuário ou a senha está incorreto.
findings.suggested: O nome de usuário ou a senha estão incorretos.

findings.issue: ちょっといいですか？ is a polite permission question ('do you have a moment?'); 'Let me speak.' turns it into a command-like statement, contradicting the record's own expl ('may I speak?') and the pt ('Posso falar um instante?').
findings.suggested: Can I talk to you for a moment?

findings.issue: 嘘などつくもんか is an indignant rhetorical denial (もんか, the sentence's grammar target). 'I won't lie.' reads as a plain statement of intent — and colloquially as the English hedge 'to be honest' — losing the emphatic force that pt and lit_en render correctly.
findings.suggested: As if I would ever lie!

findings.issue: Wrong subject: 'He' contradicts en/pt/expl, which all read the sentence as first person ('I'm sure I said'). Also 'should have said' reads as deontic 'ought to have', misrepresenting the epistemic はずです the expl teaches.

The grammar target はずだ (speaker's conviction, per expl) is dropped from the natural pt, which reads as a plain past statement. The sibling sentence sent:tatoeba-3552032 renders it ('Eu tenho certeza de que disse...'); this one should too.
findings.suggested: Tenho certeza de que mandei você cair fora.

findings.issue: Note mislabels the stem token 言っ as 'forma た (passado) de 言う', but た is tokenized separately (token 3), so 言っ alone is not the past form. sent:tatoeba-3552032 words the same token correctly (connective form, base for past た). Fix the en note likewise.
findings.suggested: forma conectiva 言っ de 言う, base para o passado た

findings.issue: pt-BR note uses 'conetiva' — European Portuguese (post-AO90) spelling or a typo; Brazilian Portuguese is 'conectiva', as used in sibling records (e.g. sent:tatoeba-3552032 'raiz conectiva').
findings.current: raiz conetiva (連用形) de 開く, ligada a そう
findings.suggested: raiz conectiva (連用形) de 開く, ligada a そう

findings.issue: Gloss ends with a dangling, truncated parenthetical '(marker of)' — an incomplete phrase shown to learners.
findings.current: there is not, does not exist (marker of)
findings.suggested: there is not, does not exist

findings.issue: Same truncation as the en gloss: dangling '(sinal de)' with nothing after 'de'.
